A formula you can implement is a formula you understand. This lab builds
surprisal and entropy in a notebook, from the definitions alone.

## What you will build

Two functions over a probability vector — the surprisal of each outcome and
the entropy of the whole distribution — plus a short argument about where
entropy is largest.

## Exercises

<Exercise>
Before opening the notebook: what is the surprisal of an event with
probability 1?

<Solution>
Zero bits: $-\log_2 1 = 0$.
</Solution>
</Exercise>

<References>
1. C. E. Shannon, "A Mathematical Theory of Communication," 1948.
</References>
